abstract: Image under low light illuminations often shows the features of low contrast, color distortion, less brightness and a considerable amount of noise. A number of image enhancement algorithms have been used for illuminating these images to obtain a highly improved and enhanced images. In this paper few existing enhancement methods based on histogram equalization, frequency domain method, retinex method, gray transformation method, image fusion method and image defogging method have been implemented to do the analysis. abstract: According to the NHS UK study, 50 % of all radiographic screenings are chest X-rays. With the aid of X-rays, specialists have had a difficult time identifying multivariate illnesses while detecting diverse disorders. Due to abnormal changes in the environment, the 21st century is the epidemic period. In the next three to four decades, global epidemics such as CORONA are likely to occur often. As a result of the coronavirus outbreak, healthcare organizations throughout Britain have indicated that over 600,000 patients are awaiting med-tech scans. In this situation, a substantial majority of X-rays are required immediately to accurately diagnose the issue. To investigate this potential, a pilot ai - powered program has been created that can diagnose sixteen among the most prominent cardiac anomalies from a patient’s chest x-ray. Based on a chest X-ray analysis, the current AI system will give a coherent answer for healthcare professionals to diagnose sixteen illnesses.

articleTitle: A Novel Energy-Efficient Offloading Protocol for UAV NOMA Mobile Edge Computing Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) are two breakthrough technologies in mobile communications and wireless networks. In this study, we investigated an energy-guaranteed offloading model based on NOMA combined with mobile edge computing (MEC) networks and UAV over the Rayleigh fading channel. The proposed model consists of a UAV that needs to offload tasks to two access points (APs) using downlink NOMA. Accordingly, we proposed a four-phase protocol, namely LEOP, to ensure system latency and energy efficiency. We derive the closed-form expression of energy-guaranteed successful computation probability (ESCP), to evaluate system performance. We employ Monte-Carlo simulations to validate our mathematical analysis by evaluating system performance under various conditions, including average transmit SNR, power allocation coefficient, task division ratio, system block time, and UAV altitude.

articleTitle: A Review on Alzheimer Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating neurological disorder that progressively worsens cognitive function and memory. Early detection is critical to avoiding worse symptoms. While computational approaches have been used to identify Alzheimer's disease, they do have drawbacks. Predicting AD in its early stages is challenging but critical for effective therapy. Machine Learning (ML) offers the potential for improving AD. We want to learn more about how machine learning might help with early AD diagnosis, perhaps revolutionizing patient treatment, by reviewing significant studies. ML provides hope by analysing complicated data patterns and improving our capacity to detect AD sooner, resulting in better patient outcomes. Out of 432 total papers in total selected 15 papers were for this review analysis from different databases like IEEE, Web of Science, etc. using keywords like "Alzheimer", "Machine Learning" etc. In this paper, a case study is also being added for the Support Vector Machine which has given an accuracy of 89%.

articleTitle: Efficient Deep Learning Models for Emotion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Social media platforms like Twitter have become significant sources of real-time data for emotion detection. With the proliferation of user-generated content, understanding the emotions expressed in tweets has become increasingly important for various applications, including marketing, public opinion analysis, and mental health monitoring. In this study, we present a comprehensive approach to emotion detection on a Twitter dataset using various machine learning and deep learning models. The models employed include Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Bidirectional GRU, to classify the tweets into different emotional categories, such as joy, love, anger, sadness, fear, and surprise. The proposed approach is evaluated using standard metrics such as model accuracy, model loss, precision, recall, and F1-score. Experimental results highlight the effectiveness of our approach in accurately detecting emotions expressed in Twitter data. The findings of this study contribute to the advancement of emotion detection techniques, providing valuable insights into understanding the dynamics of emotions in social media conversations.

articleTitle: Studying Dengue spread using Climatic conditions and Machine learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Dengue is one of the serious mosquito-borne disease, which causes flu-like symptoms like high fever, sever headache, pain in joint, muscles, eyes etc. It is suggested to control mosquito populations in an area to avoid the disease. Our research aims on identifying climatic conditions which influence mosquito population to grow rapidly in an area, and find a machine learning algorithm that best predicts dengue risk in an area based on these climatic conditions. The dataset used was sourced from kaggle.com, in which after data cleaning we implemented algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbor, Logistic regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes and Random Forest on the cleaned dataset. Each algorithm was evaluated and compared on the basis of accuracy and confusion matrix out of which K-Nearest neighbor gave best results with 99.00% accuracy while offering superior performance in confusion matrix respectively, also Temperature, Humidity and Wind displayed best relation with spread of dengue diseases among other climatic conditions.

articleTitle: Self-Driving Car
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Self-driving cars represent a revolutionary innovation poised to transform transportation systems worldwide. At their core, these autonomous vehicles leverage cutting-edge sensors like LiDAR, radar, cameras, and GPS, integrated with sophisticated AI algorithms to perceive their surroundings and navigate roads without human intervention. The true power lies in machine learning capabilities that process vast sensor data in real-time, enabling intelligent driving decisions for a safer, more efficient mobility experience. However, regulatory frameworks, ethical considerations around decision-making, cybersecurity risks, and environmental factors pose significant challenges. Despite this, the potential benefits are substantial, including increased safety by mitigating human error, enhanced accessibility for underserved populations, reduced parking needs, and environmental sustainability. As technological advancements continue, self-driving cars could usher in a new era where intelligent mobility systems coexist harmoniously with society, redefining the future of transportation globally. Overcoming hurdles through ongoing innovation and collaborative efforts between industry, policymakers, and the public will be crucial for realizing the full transformative potential of this groundbreaking technology.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based model for early detection of disease in Apple Leap and Fruit
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Diseases that affect apple quality and productivity provide difficulties for apple growers in areas like Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. In order to achieve early detection of diseases and prevention, this study presents a unique Apple Leaf and Fruit Disease Prediction (ALFDP) architecture specifically designed for Kashmiri apple leaves. We created and contrasted three models using a specific dataset that included 384 training and 98 validation pictures from three different illness classes: independent LSTM, hybrid CNN with LSTM, and CNN. With a validation accuracy of 96% and a test accuracy of 97%, the CNN model performed well. On the other hand, the hybrid CNN and LSTM model performed better, with a validation accuracy of 98% and a test accuracy of 99%. Our research demonstrates how hybrid designs may improve the precision of disease identification, providing a viable option for in-the-moment disease monitoring in apple orchards.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Machine Learning in Personalized Education Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: The traditional education system or in-person classroom teaching operates on the concept of a uniform approach for all and does not take into account the varied needs of learners, which results in a decrease in student performance. Recognizing the limitations of a one-size-fits-all approach, personalized learning systems aim to tailor educational content to each student's unique needs. This has been significantly bolstered by the recent surge in machine learning integration within education. Machine learning algorithms can now analyze student data and learning patterns, allowing educators to create highly personalized learning experiences that cater to individual strengths and weaknesses. This means learning content is designed and recommended to a learner according to the learners’ level. This research delves into the transformative impact of machine learning on traditional classroom teaching. By analyzing its implementation in personalized education systems, the paper explores how this technology can empower learning. However, it also critically examines the challenges that arise, such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, and ethical considerations. Ultimately, the goal is to ensure responsible and equitable access to this transformative technology within education.

publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Weather uncertainty poses significant challenges to industries, including construction, major events (e.g., Wimbledon, IPL), and public health (e.g., heat events) this paper addresses these challenges by a new solution that introduces an "automated weather forecast station". Leverages IoT) technology The system uses advanced forecasting techniques such as ARIMA (Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average) and deep learning to provide real-time weather data These by continuously collecting data from resources controlling the environmental sensors that have been deployed within a specific area It meets objectives and then the collected data is processed and made available through a user-friendly interface. While the concept of IoT-based weather forecasting is not new, this research goes beyond traditional applications. It extends its utility to smart cities and diverse industries, making it a valuable resource for individuals, organizations and government departments. By addressing climate-related challenges first, the program ensures safety and resilience in the face of climate change. The paper highlights the potential of these new solutions to improve decision-making processes, reduce climate-related problems, and enhance overall quality of life in urban and industrial settings as the world faces climate uncertainty increasing emphasis.

articleTitle: Ownership Structure’s effect on Dividend Policy: A Study of Selected Indian Private Sector Banks*
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Dividend distribution decisions are crucial elements of business policy and have been identified as a topic of interest in financial literature. The dividend, which serves as remuneration for stockholders' assumption of risk and investment, relies on various factors. The objective of this study is to analyze the impact of ownership structure on the ratio of dividends paid out by a company. The ownership structure is a crucial determinant of a firm's overall well-being. The current investigation was of a causal nature. The study will analyze the link in the Indian setting, using a sample of 10 private sector banks. Data will be gathered for the preceding 11 years, spanning from 2010 to 2021. The topic of sampling will be discussed. The factors to consider include the dividend pay-out ratio, the promoter's ownership, the holding of foreign institutional investors (FIIs), the holding of domestic institutional investors (DIIs), and the shareholding by the general public. Stationary test, actual fitted residual analysis, heteroskedasticity test, and histogram normality test were conducted. A multiple regression analysis is conducted on the sample companies to test the hypothesis. The results indicate that the ownership pattern has a substantial influence on the dividend policy.

articleTitle: Weapon Detection from images using YOLO and OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Gun violence incidents have sadly claimed many lives annually, making them a major global problem. A completely automated, computer-based approach for identifying popular weaponry, like rifles and pistols, is presented in this paper. Recent advances in deep learning and transfer learning technology have transformed object identification and recognition capabilities. Our suggested method makes use of the YOLO v5 (You Only Look Once) object detection model, which was trained on a private dataset made up of pictures of different types of guns. One important benefit of our methodology is that it incorporates transfer learning techniques, which removes the requirement for powerful GPUs or large amounts of processing power that are normally needed for training deep neural networks from the beginning. The outcomes show that the YOLO v5 model outperforms both conventional convolutional neural network models and its predecessor, YOLO v4. This concept could potentially help avoid killings and mass shootings by being integrated into monitoring systems, thus saving lives. Additionally, our model and methodology have the potential for the creation of robotic security devices that can identify lethal weapons and lessen the likelihood of an attack, improving public safety in high-risk regions. The potential consequences of properly and efficiently identifying firearms in real-time video feeds could be extensive, affecting public safety protocols, private security companies, and law enforcement organizations.

articleTitle: Vitiligo Image Segmentation Using Segment Anything Model
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Introducing a unique promptable segmentation task to enable zero-shot picture segmentation through two basic modes: automated everything and human prompt (e.g., points and boxes), the Segment Anything Model (SAM) is a trailblazing foundation model for universal image segmentation. SAM has proven to be highly effective in a variety of natural image segmentation tasks. Nevertheless, because of its complicated modalities, fine anatomical structures, ambiguous and complex object borders, and various object scales, using it for vitiligo image segmentation (VIS) [18] poses more difficulties. Reducing annotation time and improving visual image analysis are potential benefits of achieving zero-shot and efficient VIS. As a result, SAM becomes a potentially useful technique, and its effectiveness must be confirmed on big datasets of vitiligo images. Three open source datasets were gathered and arranged for this work, which produced a large medical segmentation dataset with 834 photos of healthy skin and 368 images of skin damaged by vitiligo. Using the Vitiligo dataset, an extensive analysis of several SAM testing procedures is carried out. Numerous tests demonstrate that SAM performs better in prompt mode than in everything mode when given manual suggestions, like boxes and points, for object recognition in vitiligo images. Furthermore, in certain photos, SAM performs admirably, while in other cases, it performs poorly or fails. Lastly, a study of the effects of several variables on SAM’s segmentation effectiveness is provided.

articleTitle: Building Futuristic Development through organization culture transformation and (DEI) Strategies at Workplace
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: The present paper investigates the intricate relationship between diversity and inclusion strategies in the workplace and their subsequent impact on organisational culture. Acknowledging the increasing recognition of the importance of diversity in contemporary workplaces, the research aims to delve into the nuanced ways in which tailored strategies can influence and shape the overall culture of an organization. The primary objectives of this research are to explore how diversity and inclusion strategies are currently implemented across various industries, understand the perceived effectiveness of these strategies, and assess their direct influence on shaping organisational culture. By examining these objectives, the study aims to contribute valuable insights to the ongoing discourse on fostering inclusive workplaces. To achieve these objectives, a structured questionnaire method was employed as the primary data collection tool.The questionnaire was designed to capture qualitative and quantitative data on the implementation of diversity and inclusion strategies, employees' perceptions of their efficacy, and the observed impact on organizational culture. The targeted sample comprises employees at different hierarchical levels across diverse industries, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the subject matter. In conclusion, this study utilizes a robust research methodology to explore the critical link between diversity and inclusion strategies and organisational culture.The findings are anticipated to contribute not only to academic knowledge but also to inform practical strategies for fostering inclusive workplaces and cultivating a positive organisational culture.

articleTitle: Detection of DDoS Attacks in Cloud Computing Environments Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Technological Innovations and Advance Computing (TIACOMP)
abstract: Cloud computing represents a paradigm shift in IT technology, providing end users with flexible, virtualized on-demand services that offer greater efficiency, reduced downtime, and lowered infrastructure costs. However, Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks remain a substantial threat to cloud reliability, causing severe damage and disruption. In DDoS attacks, perpetrators exploit compromised computers to inundate victim cloud infrastructures with packet streams, exploiting known or unknown vulnerabilities. These attacks can consume a substantial measure of the victim's network bandwidth utilization and server consumption time, significantly impacting performance. To mitigate the DDoS threat, this study proposes a detection method based on Random Forest Classifier and logistic regression algorithms. The Random Forest Classifier, when combined with detection algorithms, offers efficient DDoS attack detection. Evaluation results demonstrate substantial performance improvements in terms of precision, F1-score, sensitivity, and compared to several existing DDoS attack detection methods using real datasets.
